Roofing in Cedar Hill, Texas

Cedar Hill is high ground for North Texas, with cedar-covered slopes and Joe Pool Lake below. When a roof up here needs work, one free call connects you with an independent roofing company that takes Cedar Hill jobs.

Call (469) 649-7066 Cedar Hill permit facts
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Cedar Hill

The high ground of Dallas County

Most of North Texas is flat. Cedar Hill is not. The city sits on the escarpment that rises along the southwest side of Dallas County; the city's own nature page gives its elevation as 880 feet, the highest point in Dallas County, and city planning documents place Cedar Hill at the northern end of the Balcones Escarpment.

Below the ridge lies Joe Pool Lake, with Cedar Hill State Park on its shore. Texas Parks and Wildlife says the state acquired the park in 1982 and opened it in 1991. Next to it, Dallas County's Cedar Mountain Preserve holds some of the highest points in the county, and Dogwood Canyon Audubon Center sits alongside. Most of Cedar Hill is in Dallas County, with a small southern piece in Ellis County. The 2020 census counted 49,148 residents.

Roofing in Cedar Hill, TX is shaped by that setting: wooded slopes, homes tucked among trees, and a town that has been in the path of North Texas storms since before the Civil War.

Four reasons Cedar Hill homeowners call about roofs

Limbs over the roof

The hills and preserves that make Cedar Hill green also put branches over a lot of roofs. Rubbing limbs wear shingles, and a heavy one can come down in a storm. A roofer can point out where limbs touch; a tree service cuts them.

Leaves and valleys

Leaves and needles settle in roof valleys and gutters, hold water against the roof and slow drainage. Ask a roofer to check valleys and gutters on any inspection, not just the open field of shingles.

Spring hail

Cedar Hill shares the spring storm season of the rest of Dallas County, when hail comes through most years. Once the ice melts, dents on the gutters, the vent caps or the car hood, seen from the driveway, hint at what the shingles took.

Wind on exposed slopes

Homes on a ridge or an open slope do not have neighbors and trees blocking every gust. Ask the roofer how the shingles on your elevation will be fastened and what wind rating the product carries.

Permits and registration in Cedar Hill

Cedar Hill Building Inspections works out of the Government Center at 285 Uptown Boulevard, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Here is what the city's pages show about a roof job.

  1. Registration. The city says a person or company acting as general contractor must register with Cedar Hill, at a $100 fee for general contractors. Trades with a state license, such as electricians and plumbers, register each year with proof of that license. Roofing has no state license, so ask the roofer what it has on file with the city.
  2. The reroof permit. Residential reroof permits appear by name in the city's monthly reports of permits issued, month after month. Expect the roofer to take one out for your house and to give you the number.
  3. Inspection requests. Inspections can be requested through the online portal, by email or by phone at 972-291-5100 ext. 1093, before 4 p.m. on the day before.
  4. Questions. Building Inspections answers at 972-291-5100 ext. 1090. Fees and requirements change, so check before the job starts.

1856: the storm Cedar Hill still remembers

Cedar Hill's best known storm came early in its history. On April 29, 1856, a tornado struck the town, killing at least nine people and leaving only a building or two standing. The Dallas Herald reported on it that May, and the Dallas Pioneer history site has reprinted the account; local historians still debate whether the toll was nine or eleven.

Buildings and roofs have changed completely since then, but the season has not. Spring still brings the hail and wind that do most of the damage to Cedar Hill roofs. Searches for recent tornado damage surveys inside Cedar Hill did not turn up one, so none is claimed here.

After a storm on the hill

  • Look for limbs on the roof or hanging broken over it, and keep people and cars out from under them.
  • Check ceilings, especially near outside walls and skylights, and catch any drip.
  • Photograph the roof, gutters and yard from the ground, with the date.
  • Call your insurer to ask how the policy treats wind, hail and fallen trees, and what the deductible is.
  • Then call a roofer, and a tree service if a limb needs to come off first.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

What to ask a Cedar Hill roofer

  1. "Are you registered with Cedar Hill?" Then confirm it with Building Inspections.
  2. "Will you pull the reroof permit and send me the number?" Before tear-off, not after.
  3. "Which limbs touch my roof, and what damage have they done?" Ask for photos.
  4. "How will you fasten shingles on this slope, and what wind rating do they carry?"
  5. "Will your insurance carrier send me a certificate directly?"

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

DFW Expert Roofers is not a roofer. It does not climb, inspect, quote or pull permits. It answers your call and hands it to a roofing company that does that work.

  1. Dial the lineAn automated assistant picks up (469) 649-7066 any time and asks what you need. The same number also takes air conditioning, heating and pressure washing calls, so say "roof".

  4. Work with that companyIt inspects, prices and does the job, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it cannot pick up, it gets your name, number, town and need so it can call you back.

A limb on the roof, hail on the patio, or a drip by the skylight? Call and say so. The roofer you are connected with comes out to see it, and its estimate is its own, on paper.

Cedar Hill roofing questions

Is a reroof permit required in Cedar Hill TX?

Plan on one. The City of Cedar Hill issues residential reroof permits every month, and they show up by name in its monthly permits issued reports. A registered contractor normally applies, and inspections are requested through the city portal, by email or by phone before 4 p.m. the day before. Building Inspections is in the Government Center at 285 Uptown Boulevard, 972-291-5100 ext. 1090. Confirm the current fee there.

Do roofers have to be registered in Cedar Hill?

Cedar Hill says a person or company acting as the general contractor must register with the city, and lists a $100 fee for general contractors. Ask any roofer whether it is registered with Cedar Hill before you sign. Because Texas has no roofing license, registration is a record, not a skills test. See how to check a roofer in Texas.

Are trees a problem for roofs in Cedar Hill?

They can be. Much of Cedar Hill's character comes from wooded hills and preserves, and branches that hang over a roof can scrape shingles, hold leaves and moisture, and fall in storms. Have a roofer look at where limbs touch the roof, and hire a tree service, not yourself on a ladder, to cut them back. If a limb is already on the roof, read the emergency roof repair page.

If I call the line for roofing in Cedar Hill TX, who picks up?

An automated assistant answers DFW Expert Roofers at any hour, hears the roof trouble in your words along with your Cedar Hill street, and then transfers the call to an independent, locally owned roofing company. If that company cannot pick up, it gets your details to call back. The line itself never inspects or quotes. A roofing company may pay the line for a referral.

Roof trouble in Cedar Hill? Call free

Say what the roof is doing and which town you are in. The automated assistant passes you to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in DFW. That company comes out, looks at the roof and prices the job itself.
